title: Orbits Type
definition: An orbit is the curved path of a celestial object or spacecraft around a star, planet, or moon, dictated by gravitational forces and centrifugal balance. In space technology missions, orbit types determine a satellite's coverage, resolution, latency, and application scope ranging from Earth observation to deep-space navigation.
importanceInUpsc: Frequently tested in UPSC CSE Prelims via direct factual matching (e.g., altitude, inclination, application of LEO, MEO, GEO, SSO, and Lagrange points) and in Mains (GS Paper III: Space Technology advancements, dual-use capabilities, satellite communication security, and debris mitigation).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Orbits Type.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic Newtonian mechanics, gravitation, and relative motion
